status: Conditional first-law and real-air sensitivity; no new CFD or motor-map validation

no_load.reason: Free-running airflow and motor heat transfer are not published in the available point data. No external 840 W shaft extraction. Startup stores rotational energy; internal losses and casing heat transfer may still alter exhaust temperature.

equations.energy: T0_out = T0_in - (Wshaft - Q_into_motor)/(mdot cp), negligible potential-energy change
equations.flow: mdot = rho A U; mdot depends on inlet pressure, exhaust pressure, speed, temperature and leakage
equations.regulator: hout=hin only for negligible heat/shaft-work/kinetic changes

limits: 22 C in the tank is not automatically 22 C at the motor inlet
At a hypothetical heat-free initial 200-to-6.3 bar throttle, real-air EOS gives about -11.8 C; walls, hoses and blowdown change this
Do not extrapolate the 840 W / 19.4 g/s motor pair to that subzero inlet without a supplier map or test
The motor-inlet22 result assumes sustained catalogue power/flow and zero net heat into the motor
No-load means zero external shaft work, not necessarily exactly zero exhaust cooling; regulator cooling and casing heat remain possible
The 19.4 g/s value is already the loaded catalogue-point conversion; it is not free-running airflow
Too much load can stall the rotor; shaft power then tends to zero even if leakage continues
Path UA is inherited and unmeasured; no steady or startup thermal guarantee
Bulk energy calculation uses stagnation temperature; high-speed port static temperature may differ before diffuser recovery
Product page lists 7 bar maximum; manual says 6.3 bar or nameplate. Keep 6.3 bar running target and confirm the nameplate/pressure-reduction package
Existing saved CFD remains at 4.313/10.281 C source. No CFD at -0.461 C was run

references.title: Atlas Copco B4770001 manual: no-load hotspots, load and speed
